title: Erdos #1147: Additive Basis from Diophantine Approximation

problemStatement.formal: For irrational alpha > 0, ask whether {n >= 1 : ||alpha n^2|| < 1/log(n)} is an additive basis of order 2; Konieczny disproved this.
problemStatement.plain: Erdos asked whether integers whose alpha n^2 values lie very close to an integer always form a two-summand additive basis. Konieczny showed the answer is no.
whyMatters: Links metric Diophantine approximation with additive-combinatorial basis questions.
Shows that an infinite approximating set can still be too sparse or irregular to cover large integers by pairwise sums.
The generalized threshold result applies to any epsilon(n) tending to zero.

proven: Lean defines distance to the nearest integer, the Diophantine approximation set, generalized threshold sets, additive bases of order 2, and the sumset/cofinite equivalence.
Elementary threshold and sqrt(2) irrationality facts are proved without sorries.
The theorem erdos_1147_false derives the disproof from the sqrt2_not_basis axiom.
open: Konieczny's almost-everywhere disproof, its generalized threshold form, the sqrt(2) counterexample, and infinitude are active axioms in Lean.
The historical theorem is not rederived from measure-theoretic or equidistribution infrastructure in this file.
